reason: The cited evidence confirms that Cr coatings fail by peeling/cracking in high-temperature steam (E2) and lists CrAl as a coating strategy (E1), but neither passage provides specific evidence that Al addition forms an interfacial Al₂O₃ diffusion barrier or that such a barrier limits Cr–Zr interdiffusion. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Elemental Cr coatings on Zr-alloy cladding suffer from Cr–Zr interdiffusion at high temperatures, causing premature failure.
Aluminum can preferentially oxidize to form Al₂O₃ at elevated temperatures.
An Al₂O₃ layer can act as a diffusion barrier to inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Cr–Al alloy coatings are a known category of ATF cladding materials.
